verdict.why:
The draft is close but does not hold. Its counts and its zero-unexplained claim come from code that differs from its own written tests. Several dividing meanings fail on cases the draft neither states nor counts.

I wrote my own classifier from the tests as worded and ran it over openscriptures_strongs.jsonl. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mashiachsonyosef-github-io/c72302ec-11e7-5b6d-a5ab-47bb077585fe/scratchpad/punct/verify/openscriptures_strongs/. The main files are common.mjs, labels.mjs, classify.mjs, census.mjs, compare-counts.mjs (writes counts-own.json and counts-draft.json), division.mjs (writes v3-summary-*.json), falsify.mjs (writes falsify.json), field-misread.mjs and extras.mjs. I read nothing from the draft's ledger.mjs except three things, each used only to explain a difference: its label vocabulary (copied into labels.mjs for a separate run), its attach test at ledger.mjs:174, and its changes-vs-v3.jsonl rows.

WHAT REPRODUCES EXACTLY:
- Routes 23,646 and records 14,929: 7,503 list and 7,426 sentence.
- Slice routes on list records 0; sentence records carrying a slice 4,738.
- Route regions: 8,203 list whole, 7,515 sentence whole, 7,928 sentence slice. 91 slices sit at the first of several offsets.
- All 18 marks and 52,371 occurrences.
- These shapes match exactly:
  - commas: ie 1,072, etc 21, in_aside 759, in_group 1,289, in_note 28, between 363, last_piece 490, untagged 104
  - periods: list_end 8,190, ie 3,008, etc 61, ellipsis 148, in_note 280, in_group 15, sentence_end 10, trace_end 7, stray_for_comma 6, stray_before_comma 1
  - every semicolon, ×, +, apostrophe, bracket, !, ?, : and point shape, and the 19/16/2 unbalanced counts
- With the draft's own label list substituted: def_label 812, def_aside 2,974, labelled_alternative 130, sense_separator 2,046 and after_bare_label 3.
- The v3 comparison (run with the draft's label list) matches exactly: 23,646 compared; 18,593 same, of which 7,829 differ only by the full stop; 3,324 v3 divides / declaration whole; 163 declaration divides / v3 whole; 1,566 divided differently.
- The declaration's division: 5,026 routes divided (3,389 list, 1,637 sentence), 272 note pieces, 34 routes v3 holds damaged. Pieces: 18,795 with the draft's attach code, 18,794 by its words.
- With my own label list, the v3 comparison is 3,325 and 1,565 instead of 3,324 and 1,566.

COUNT DIFFERENCES (tests as worded, draft's label list):
- Commas: rendering_separator 11,080 vs 11,081; attaches_syllable 6 vs 5; name_then_description 2,093 vs 2,094; after_label 1,635 vs 1,657; short_series 663 vs 644; clause 291 vs 287.
- Periods: abbreviation 47 vs 54, plus 7 periods that fit no worded test.
- List parentheses: aside 59 vs 106; optional_words 1,880 vs 1,827; suffix_syllable 1,013 vs 1,022; alternatives 534 vs 531.
- Hyphens: suffix_syllable 1,327 vs 1,328, plus 1 that fits no test ("hither(-(to))").
- With my own label list the differences grow: def_label 1,055 vs 812 and def_aside 2,728 vs 2,974. The written label test ends in "..." and does not fix the set.

COMPLETENESS:
- 8 occurrences fit no worded test: 7 periods and 1 hyphen.
- The words also leave the order between overlapping tests open. Examples: period abbreviation vs aside_sentence_end overlaps 28 times; trace_end vs sentence_end 4; trace_end vs aside_sentence_end 3; tagged commas that are both ie and name 3; name and between 2.

FALSIFICATION OF DIVIDING SHAPES. Each has at least 3 attempts in falsify.mjs. These failures are not stated or counted in the declaration:
- period.list_end: 3 real renderings fall after a stray full stop and would be withheld as notes (מלה, גבולה, לודי). One "note" is damage (נתש). One note is glued into the last rendering (יעדי).
- comma.def_between_tagged_glosses: 4 commas separate a name's meaning from the name itself, not alternative renderings (בהן, זבוד, תיריא, שכרון).
- comma.rendering_separator: the draft's code prints 2 syllables as renderings, "-th" (שבע) and "-or)" (עשק). Its words would instead print "( -pied)" (מלאכה) as a piece.
- semicolon.sense_separator: 1 occurrence (מהר), where the ';' closes the label "i.e. (by implication)" instead of separating senses.
- semicolon.rendering_separator: 2 of 13 (אפרת) separate Strong's senses, because that record is the end of Strong's sentence plus the list.
- The field test, which every division depends on, reads 7 KJV list records as Strong's sentence. That leaves 15 rendering separators uncut.

Already stated or counted, and passed:
- the 82 sense pieces that open with a usage note
- the 16 lone-group pieces
- the orphan-closer refusal

The orphan closers' effect is wider than stated: 9 commas in 8 records cut one damaged group into separate "renderings".
falsified_meanings: period.list_end (divides; 'anything after it is a note'): 3 renderings after a stray stop would be withheld as notes: מלה 'commandment, matter, thing. word.'; גבולה 'border, bound, coast, landmark. place.'; לודי 'Ludim. Lydians.'. Damage taken as a note: נתש '... × utterly. s'. A note glued into the last rendering: יעדי 'Iddo (from the margin) See 3035 .'. Not stated or counted.

comma.def_between_tagged_glosses (divides; 'alternative renderings'): 4 of 363 separate the name's meaning from the name: בהן 'thumb , Bohan , an Israelite'; זבוד 'given , Zabud , an Israelite'; תיריא 'fearful , Tirja , an Israelite'; שכרון 'drunkenness , Shikkeron , a place'. Not stated.

comma.rendering_separator (divides): the draft's code (ledger.mjs:174 tests only the character right after the comma) prints syllables as renderings in 2 places: שבע '-teenth), -th, times)' and עשק 'oppress(-ion), -or)'. Read literally, the draft's words instead divide off מלאכה 'occupation, ( -pied), officer' as a rendering. Not stated.

comma.rendering_separator: 9 commas in 8 records with an orphan ')' cut the alternatives of one damaged group into 'renderings': היה 'be(-come), accomplished, committed, like)'; עת '(meal-), what) time'; also שחר, נדבה, מול. The refusal counts the 16 orphans in 15 routes but not these cuts.

semicolon.sense_separator (divides): מהר 'flow easily, i.e. (by implication) ; to hurry'. The ';' closes a label that governs the next sense, so the draft's code prints a piece ending in a dangling label. 1 occurrence, not stated. Read literally, the words would instead divide לבב 'by implication (as denominative from 3824 ); to unheart'.

semicolon.rendering_separator (divides; 'one KJV rendering from the next'): 2 of 13 in אפרת 'perhaps for Ephraim; also of an Israelitish woman; Ephrath'. That record is the end of Strong's sentence plus the list, so these two separate Strong's senses.

Field test (precedence step 1, decides which dividing shapes apply): 7 KJV list records that end in a closing note are read as Strong's sentence: יה, שיה, מצפה, דיבון, הי, שכר, ינח (7 whole routes). Their 15 depth-0 rendering separators are never cut (ינח 11, יה 2, שכר 2).

Non-dividing, given for completeness: period.abbreviation (draft count 54) includes 7 sentence-ending stops before a closing note or quote ('Mitspah. (This', "'-jah.'"). period.aside_sentence_end (29) includes 21 abbreviations ('(reflex.)', '(adj.)', '(compar.)', '(techn.)'), which contradicts the draft's own abbreviation examples. comma.def_name_then_description takes אם 'also Oh that! , when' (not a name) and עי 'Ai , Aja or Ajath' (variant names), so the between-gloss division is lost there.
corrections: Field test: let the closing note after the list's full stop be a parenthesized '( )' note or a closing quote as well as '[ ]'. Either that, or state and count the 7 list records it misreads (יה, שיה, מצפה, דיבון, הי, שכר, ינח), which leave 15 rendering separators uncut. Also count אפרת, whose record is the end of Strong's sentence plus the list.

period.list_end: state and count as exceptions, or test for, the 3 renderings after a stray stop (מלה 'word.', גבולה 'place.', לודי 'Lydians.'), the damaged trailing 's' in נתש, and the note glued into the last rendering in יעדי.

comma.def_between_tagged_glosses: do not divide when the next piece is a capitalized name followed by ' , ' and a description, the pattern '<meaning> , <Name> , <description>' (4 cases: בהן, זבוד, תיריא, שכרון). Or declare these 4 as exceptions.

comma.attaches_syllable: make the code match the words for a dash after whitespace (', -th' and ', -or)' attach). Make the words match the code for a spaced group ('( -pied)' attaches). After both fixes, no syllable prints as a rendering. Today the words give 6 attaches and 11,080 separators; the code gives 5 and 11,081.

semicolon.after_bare_label: state how the piece is bounded and that ( ) groups are stripped. Bounding it at the nearest depth-0 ',' or ';' and stripping groups gets both מהר and לבב right. The draft's code gets מהר wrong; the literal words get לבב wrong.

Usage labels: list the full label set in the declaration. The words end in '...', and def_label (812 by the draft's list vs 1,055 by mine), def_aside, labelled_alternative, after_label, short_series, clause, after_bare_label and sense_separator all depend on it. Even with the draft's list, comma.def_after_label counts 1,635 by the words against 1,657 claimed. Say whether groups inside the piece are ignored, which gives 1,659 here. Small differences remain in name (2,093 vs 2,094), short_series and clause.

Give an explicit order for overlapping tests of one mark. Definition periods: the draft's code order trace_end > aside_sentence_end > abbreviation > sentence_end files 21 abbreviations such as '(adj.)' under aside_sentence_end. Testing 'letter-word then )' as an abbreviation first fixes that. Tagged commas: ie > etc > name > between > last > untagged.
period: add a shape for a sentence-ending stop before a closing note or quote. 7 periods fit no worded test, and the draft's code files them as 'abbreviation'.

paren list tests: write in the leads the code actually uses, since the code's list_aside includes 'including', 'includ.', 'from the marg…' and 'by correction' (59 by the words vs 106 claimed). Allow a leading nested '(' or '[' for suffix_syllable (1,013 vs 1,022). The derived counts then move too: alternatives 534 vs 531, optional_words 1,880 vs 1,827.
hyphen.suffix_syllable: allow a following '(' as in 'hither(-(to))'. Under the words that hyphen fits no test.
Refusal for a closer with nothing open: count the depth-0 cuts it causes (9 commas in 8 records produce pieces like 'like)' and 'selves)'), not only the 16 orphans.

questions: 1. A comma between two tagged glosses in Strong's sentence ('to expose , dismiss ,'): 363 commas in 242 routes. Reading A (declared): it divides, because the provider tagged both sides as definition words. Reading B: each sense stays whole, because the store already carries these glosses as slice routes on the same record (the left gloss in 205 of 363, the right in 215), so dividing prints each one a second time in its sentence form ('to expose' beside 'expose').

2. A tagged gloss followed by the definition's last piece, where the tag on the right can't be seen: 490 commas in 490 routes. Reading A: it divides like question 1; the right piece is itself a slice route in 164. Reading B (declared): it stays whole, because the last piece is sometimes a qualifier ('to carve , whether wood or stone') and the characters can't tell which.

3. A name and its description ('Adar , the 12th Hebrew month'): 2,094 commas in 2,093 routes. Reading A (declared): one reading. Reading B: two readings, name and description, as today's engine prints them in 2,025 routes.

4. The list's full stop: 7,829 routes. Reading A (declared): it is the list's end mark and is not printed with the last reading ('Adar' rather than 'Adar.'). Reading B: print it as the provider wrote it; the division is the same either way.

5. The note after the list ('Compare 3402 .', 'See also 1050 .'): 272 pieces in 272 routes. Of these, 255 open with See or Compare, 3 are parenthesized, and 14 open otherwise; one of those, 'raphah, Raphah. See 7497 ...', holds renderings. Reading A (declared): the note is its own piece, marked as a note and never offered as a reading. Reading B: it stays on the last rendering as today ('Jareb. Compare 3402 .' as one reading).

6. A sense after ';' that opens with a usage note ('but used only adverbially ...', 'used adverbially, in mourning weeds'): 82 of 2,046 senses. Reading A (declared): a sense, printed as a reading. Reading B: a note on the sense before it, kept with that sense.

7. A KJV list item that is a group alone ('(perplexed)', '( well)', '(meal-)'): 16 pieces. Reading A (declared): a piece of its own. Reading B: notation for the rendering beside it. Either way it is never joined here; re-cutting is the store's job at the provider's characters.

8. Damaged routes: today's gloss-store drops a sense with unbalanced parentheses from the pool, and 34 routes carry one (19 list, 10 sentence, 5 slice). Under the August rule as declared here, 21 of them divide up to the unclosed opener and the rest print whole. Which behavior should the page have?
